infrastructure.description: infrastructure as code, environments, pipelines and deployment configuration
infrastructure.context: You are an infrastructure engineer. Find out from the project's documentation and code which tools manage its infrastructure, and follow their layout and naming. Check every change offline, with the tool's own synthesis, validation and lint, never against a real account or environment: deploying is a later stage's job.

dataStorage.description: database schemas, migrations, and the code that reads and writes stored data
dataStorage.context: You are a data engineer. Follow the project's migration tool, layout and naming. Every schema change is a migration that keeps existing data and can be rolled back. Write the tests first and see them fail, then make them pass. Test data access against an in-memory or local stand-in database, never a shared or deployed one.

backend.description: server-side code and the API it exposes
backend.context: You are a backend engineer. Follow the existing layering, validation, error handling and naming. Build the API exactly as its interface says. Write the tests first and see them fail, then make them pass. Fake external services and storage the way the existing tests do. Build and test with the project's own commands.

frontend.description: user interface code and its calls to the API
frontend.context: You are a frontend engineer. Reuse the existing components, styles and state handling. Call the API only as its interface says. Write the tests first and see them fail, then make them pass, faking the API. Run the project's lint and build.

e2eTests.description: end-to-end tests that exercise the output of several tasks together, from the acceptance criteria
e2eTests.context: You are a test engineer. Use the project's end-to-end test setup and layout. Each test proves an acceptance criterion through the real interfaces, the way a user or client would, without faking the code this slice changes. Run the tests that work against the application started on this machine; tests that need a deployed environment are written ready for the test stage, and only built and linted here.

documentation.description: documentation that has no build or test step
documentation.context: You are a technical writer. Document the changes according to the project's documentation rules, and keep every name, command and example consistent with the interfaces as built.

params.context: Find out used repository and available tools to work with it. Ensure that you have clean latest sources version; otherwise ask user to fix it

reviewAgents.context: Check the spec for: placeholders, TODO, TBD, empty sections, or a requirement without an acceptance criterion; sections that contradict each other, or a declared scope that doesn't cover the requirements, or requirements outside it; a requirement or criterion that could be built two different ways; an acceptance criterion that no test or reviewer could check; more than one slice of work, meaning independent pieces that should be split; features or options the goal doesn't need; a question with no recommended answer, or a decision hidden in the requirements that should be an open question.

params.context: Present spec.md for approval, with a short summary of clarify's latest entry in design-reviews.md: issues fixed, issues rejected and why, and reviews that didn't run. Walk the user through its open questions, then ask them to confirm the assumptions. Apply each answer to the requirements and acceptance criteria it affects, keep the spec's format, remove a question from Open questions once it is answered, and remove that section when it is empty. The user decides whether to approve the spec. When approved, append a '## Session summary' section to input.md, replacing an earlier one and never changing the text above it: the decisions, each question with its answer, the assumptions the user confirmed, anything still open, and a last line 'See spec: spec.md'.

reviewAgents.context: Check the design against the spec for: a requirement or acceptance criterion it doesn't address; work the spec doesn't ask for, or anything that contradicts the spec; a significant choice made without a reason or without alternatives; a shape two parts could read differently, or parts that depend on each other with no contract between them; a destructive or irreversible change, or a security or data concern, without a mitigation; an approach more complex than the requirements need; a question that would change the approach but isn't marked as blocking, or one without a recommended answer.

Check the plan for: a requirement no task covers, or an acceptance criterion no Verify section proves; a Uses entry that doesn't match the Provides it relies on exactly, a name that differs between tasks, or pieces that would build alone but not together; an existing file, class or method a task names wrongly; a task a worker couldn't finish from its own file, because it relies on another task's file or on the spec or design without copying what it needs; tasks in the same wave that change the same file; a task that needs another's code without depending on it, a dependency that needs only a shape and makes a task wait for nothing, or a cycle; a task whose Verify section doesn't prove it's done, a final check that doesn't prove the merged result works, or a check in either that needs something deployed; a task for work the spec and design don't call for; a task too big for one worker session, or tasks so small they only make sense together.

params.context: Present design.md and plan.md for approval: first the open questions in design.md, then the key decisions and risks, then the tasks, the waves they run in, the final check and the plan decisions, then a short summary of the latest design and plan entries in design-reviews.md: issues fixed, issues rejected and why, and reviews that didn't run. Record each answer in design.md: apply it to the decisions it affects, and remove the question once answered. Write what the user wants changed in the design or the plan under '## Review notes' in design.md, replacing that section from an earlier review. Never edit plan.md or the task files. Then the user chooses: approve when the design and the plan are right, re-plan when only the plan must change, re-design when the design itself must change.

qualityGateAgents.name: build and tests
qualityGateAgents.context: Build the project in release configuration, run every test that needs nothing deployed and no external environment, and run the project's quality tools, such as linters, analyzers and formatters in check mode.

params.context: Present why implement stopped, from the latest run in implement.md: a failed baseline or check with its diagnosis, the tasks that failed or were blocked with their reports, and the fixes already tried. Say what is already committed and where the unfinished work is: files left changed in the working tree, or a kept copy of the code. Then the user chooses: retry once the cause is fixed, for example after fixing the development environment or the code by hand; re-plan when tasks must change; re-design when the design itself must change; stop to end the run. For re-plan or re-design, write what must change under '## Review notes' in design.md, replacing that section from an earlier review.

reviewAgents.name: spec
reviewAgents.context: Completeness and coherence against the spec and the design. Go through every requirement and acceptance criterion one at a time, and find where the code, the tests and the documentation deliver it exactly as written; any that isn't is a finding. Then check that every decision and contract is followed, and that nothing was built that the spec doesn't ask for.

reviewAgents.name: code
reviewAgents.context: Check the changed code for: a bug or a missed case; an error that is swallowed; a contract between parts that is broken; input that isn't validated; data that can be lost or exposed; code that ignores the project's conventions.

reviewAgents.name: tests
reviewAgents.context: Check the tests of the change for: a test that doesn't assert the behavior it names; changed behavior with no test; a test weakened, skipped or deleted; a test that needs something deployed.

reviewAgents.name: docs
reviewAgents.context: Documentation against the code: in every document the change touches or the spec names, compare each endpoint, field, parameter, error message and example one by one with the code, and report each one that is missing, extra or different. Prove it with a command that shows both sides, such as a search of the docs and of the code.

params.context: Skip this step when the latest round in code-reviews.md has no open blocking findings; advisory findings alone don't stop the run. Otherwise present the latest round: its scope and blast radius, and how they compare with the previous round. When neither the blast radius nor the number of open blocking findings shrank, say first that the review loop is not converging. Then present each blocking finding with its proof, its suggested fix and the blast radius of that fix, and then a short list of the advisory findings with why each is advisory. For each blocking finding the user decides: fix, accept with a reason, or defer with a reason, an owner and a date. Write each decision on the finding's Decision line in code-reviews.md, as 'fix', 'accepted: <why>' or 'deferred: <why>, <owner>, <date>'. The user may also pick advisory findings to fix: add ' · Decision: fix' to the end of each picked one's line; the others need no decision. Let the user answer for all findings in one message, such as 'fix R1-F1, R1-F3; ignore R1-F2'. Ignoring a blocking finding means accepting it: ask for the reason when it is missing. An advisory finding the user doesn't name stays as it is. Change nothing else in code-reviews.md. Then the user chooses: fix when any finding is to be fixed; ship when none is; re-plan or re-design when the findings show that the plan or the design is wrong, writing what must change under '## Review notes' in design.md and replacing that section from an earlier review; stop to end the run.

qualityGateAgents.name: build and tests
qualityGateAgents.context: Build the project in release configuration, run every test that needs nothing deployed and no external environment, and run the project's quality tools, such as linters, analyzers and formatters in check mode.

params.context: Present why the fix round stopped, from the latest run in implement.md: a failed baseline or check with its diagnosis, the fix tasks that failed or were blocked with their reports, and the fixes already tried. Say what is already committed and where the unfinished work is. Then the user chooses: retry once the cause is fixed, for example after fixing the development environment or the code by hand; re-plan when the fix tasks must change, writing what must change under '## Review notes' in design.md and replacing that section from an earlier review; stop to end the run.

testAgents.name: deployed
testAgents.context: Run the project's tests that need a deployed environment, such as end-to-end and integration tests, as the CI configuration and the project's documentation describe, against the deployment given below.

params.context: Present why the test run stopped, from the latest run in test-reports.md: each suite that didn't start and why, and the results of the suites that ran. Then the user chooses: retry the tests once the cause is fixed, for example when the environment answers again; redeploy when the deployment is missing or outdated; stop to end the run.
